summary: Raven Roost, a 1934 L-4 cab in Yakima County, was abandoned by 1956 and removed around 1964 for microwave radio facilities that still occupy the summit.

facts.status_note: Cab removed around 1964; communications towers now stand on the summit, and no source describes what remains of the cab
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Wenatchee National Forest (Naches Ranger District)

access.note: Reached by Forest Service road; snow can drift across the road until about July 1. Potable water is not available at the trailhead.

visit.trail_note: The Raven Roost Trail starts at the high point at road's end; a free wilderness permit is required at the Norse Peak trailhead

events.note: L-4 cab built on the ground; WillhiteWeb credits the Civilian Conservation Corps and a narrow one-way road
Panoramic photos taken in August 1934; captions give both the 16th and the 18th
Dick Simmons was the last person to man the lookout
Cab removed around 1964 to make room for microwave radio facilities; the register says the mid-1960s
Registered August 15, 2012 as FFLOS US 1379; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register pages say abandoned by 1956, while WillhiteWeb says the last person to man the lookout was there in 1962. The 1956 date may mark the end of routine use, with the cab staffed only in high fire danger until 1962.
Register and WillhiteWeb both date the cab to 1934; the photo captions in the sources give August 16 in one place and August 18 in another.

notes_for_editor: Build year (1934) and removal (mid-1960s to around 1964) agree across sources. Staffing end is disputed: register 1956 vs WillhiteWeb last-manned 1962. Today's summit description rests on WillhiteWeb's 2016 photos and text, so it may be out of date. Access level 'public' is inferred from the Forest Service road and the WillhiteWeb drive-up note; the access note records the seasonal snow. Photo captions disagree on the 1934 panorama day (16th vs 18th). No new photos added.
